service.description: The current user's notifications, newest first, with their topic, inbox, reason, record, actor and app, and the counts the screens show beside them. Filters: inboxEnumId (NinNotifications by default; 'all' for both), reasonEnumId, appName, topic, viewed (N unread, Y read, empty both), fromDate and thruDate (on sentDate), text (in the title, ignoring case) and approvals (only the approvals waiting: unviewed, of a topic with an approve service).

parameter.name: viewed
parameter.description: N for the unread, Y for the read, empty for both

parameter.name: unreadCounts
parameter.description: The unread of each inbox, by inboxEnumId

parameter.name: reasonCounts
parameter.description: The unread of the inbox by reasonEnumId ('' for none)

parameter.name: appCounts
parameter.description: The unread of the inbox by appName ('' for none)

service.description: Mark the current user's notifications viewed: those of notificationMessageIdList, or, without one, all of the user's unviewed, of one inbox when inboxEnumId is given, except the approvals waiting (notifications of a topic with an approve service), which are decided, not read. Only the user's own rows change.

parameter.name: notificationMessageId
parameter.description: One id, as a list of one

parameter.name: inboxEnumId
parameter.description: Without ids: NinNotifications or NinUpdates; empty for all

service.description: The current user's decision on a notification that asks for one (IronStone R23): the topic's approveServiceName is called, as the user, with recordEntityName, recordId, message (the messageJson as a Map) and notificationMessageId; its results are returned. The user must be a recipient (NotificationMessageUser). On success the decision is final for the message: every recipient's row is marked viewed, so it leaves the approvals waiting of all of them (an approval each of several users decides is a message per user); the service's errors are the caller's messages and nothing is marked.

As approve#NotificationMessage, with the topic's refuseServiceName, which also gets reason. When the topic has refuseReasonRequired=Y a refuse without a reason is an error; otherwise the refuse service decides whether it needs one.
The body of approve#NotificationMessage and refuse#NotificationMessage.

The daily digest (a ServiceJob): for each user who has the digest on for a topic (NotificationTopicUser.digest=Y, or NotificationTopic.digestDefault=Y and no user row that says N), one email of their unviewed notifications on those topics sent in the last hours, that no email carried yet (neither the immediate email of a topic the user gets by email, nor an earlier digest); each goes in one digest at most (NotificationMessageUser.digestDate). The job is hourly; a user is sent only in the hour of their NOTIFICATION_DIGEST_HOUR preference (0–23, missing means 6) in their time zone. A user who cannot be signed in (disabled, terminated) or has no email address is passed over; a failing user is logged and the others still get theirs.

parameter.name: ignoreHour
parameter.description: When true, send whatever the hour (a test). The scheduled job leaves this false.

parameter.name: userCount
parameter.description: The users a digest was sent to

service.description: One user's digest, for send#NotificationDigests: with nobody signed in (the job) the session takes the user's time zone and locale, so the dates are the user's (the machine's zone when the account has none); sends the template with notificationList, notificationCount, userId and userFullName as its body parameters; and sets digestDate (and emailMessageId, when the email is saved) on each NotificationMessageUser row it carried. Unless ignoreHour, it sends only when the local hour is the user's NOTIFICATION_DIGEST_HOUR (0–23, missing means 6), read from UserPreference by userId (the job is not signed in as them), and a skipped hour marks nothing. A disabled or terminated account gets none.
